newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber closes steady in thin dealings.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber closes steady in thin dealings.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market finished flat on Monday in thin trade with most consumers sitting on the sidelines, dealers said.
"It's the Monday blues. The major consumers were pretty much on the sidelines. It's been very slow going today. We'll see how it goes again tomorrow," a trader said.
"It's flat. The only buying we saw was when some local people did some covering in the ring sessions," a dealer said.
Most of the industry were also said to be out of the market as they were already at meetings of the International Rubber Study Group and at the annual rubber trade forum in Liverpool.
"Some guys have already flown to Britain. We may be in for a very slow week," one dealer said.
Traders said the market was also waiting for any news of any possible deal by the Thai government, which is spending one billion baht to prop up rubber prices.
Higher prices in Japan failed to inspire the market, with most finishing easier in light dealings.
At 0945 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 115.25 U.S. cents a kg from 115.50 cents. July RSS1 was seen at 163.00 Singapore cents (US$1.14) a kg from 164.25 cents.
